Check2DRequest.description:
A 2D layout to check: the `solve_2d` request it answers, unchanged, and a
successful `solve_2d` response -- one the engine returned, or one written
elsewhere in the same shape. Only its `placements` and `unplaced` are
judged.

Check3DRequest.description:
A 3D packing to check: the `solve_3d` request it answers, unchanged, and a
successful `solve_3d` response. Only its `placements` and `unplaced` are
judged.

CheckResponse.description:
Whether a layout or packing keeps every rule of its problem, and each rule
it breaks; or, with `success: false`, why the request was refused.

code.description: The refusal's stable reason, when `success` is `false`.

success.description:
Whether the check ran; `false` with `error` / `code` / `details` when the
request was refused.

max_generations.description:
GA/BRKGA generation budget: a whole number from 0 to 4294967295.
Omitted, each strategy uses the budget it is tuned for (see
`Config::max_generations`).

max_iterations.description:
SA/GDRR/ALNS iteration budget: a whole number, at least 1. Omitted,
each strategy uses the budget it is tuned for (see
`Config::max_iterations`).

multi_sheet.description:
Distribute overflow across multiple sheets (2D only).

When `true`, parts that do not fit on a single sheet spill onto additional
sheets instead of becoming unplaced. `sheets_used` then reports the sheet
count and each placement's `sheet_index` selects its sheet; placement
coordinates are sheet-local (relative to each sheet's origin). Defaults to
`false` (single-sheet solve).

population_size.description:
GA/BRKGA population size: a whole number, at least 2. Omitted, each
strategy uses the size it is tuned for (see `Config::population_size`).

seed.description:
Optional RNG seed for reproducible stochastic runs (GA, BRKGA, SA,
GDRR, ALNS): a whole number from 0 to 18446744073709551615. A seeded
run that ends on its own budget, not on the time limit, is reproduced
exactly (see `Config::seed`).

strategy.description:
Optimization strategy, by name (case-insensitive); the strategies
offered in each dimension are listed by `available_strategies`.

target_utilization.description:
Target utilization (0.0 - 1.0): ga, brkga and sa stop once every piece
is placed at this utilization or more. Refused (`invalid_option`)
under any other strategy.

time_limit_ms.description: Time limit in milliseconds: a whole number, at least 0 (0 = no limit).

CutStepResponse.description: A single step in the cutting sequence.

instance.description: Instance index of the placed geometry.

rapid_from.description: Starting point of rapid move [x, y] (null for first step).

cut_speed.description: Machine cutting speed (units/s). For time estimation only.

exterior_direction.description: Default cut direction for exterior contours: "ccw", "cw", or "auto".

home_position.description: Home position [x, y] for the cutting head.

interior_direction.description: Default cut direction for interior contours: "ccw", "cw", or "auto".

kerf_width.description: Kerf width (cutting tool width). Set to 0.0 to disable kerf compensation.

max_2opt_iterations.description:
Maximum number of 2-opt improvement iterations: a whole number, at
least 0.

pierce_candidates.description:
Number of candidate pierce points per contour: a whole number, at
least 1.

pierce_weight.description: Weight factor for pierce count in cost function.

rapid_speed.description: Machine rapid traverse speed (units/s). For time estimation only.

time_limit_ms.description:
Wall-clock budget (ms) for the 2-opt improvement phase. `0` = unlimited.
Prevents the sequencing pass from blocking the caller (e.g. the browser
main thread) on large inputs. Defaults to 5000 when omitted.

cutting_config.description: Cutting path configuration (optional; defaults will be used if absent).

geometries.description: Original geometry definitions (same format as nesting request).

solve_result.description: Solve result from a previous nesting operation.

code.description:
Stable name of the reason a request was refused
(`parameter_out_of_range`, `invalid_geometry`, `duplicate_id`, ...);
`null` on success. Branch on this, not on `error`, whose wording may
change.

details.description:
The values behind `code` -- the setting, the geometry id, the
positions; `null` on success.

estimated_time_seconds.description:
Estimated total time in seconds: the rapid distance at `rapid_speed`
plus the cut distance at `cut_speed` (0 when nothing is cut, and on
error responses).

skipped_contours.description:
Contours of placed parts that the plan cannot cut, and why. A part
listed here is not fully cut by `sequence`.

Dimension.description:
The two problem families a strategy runs on: 2D nesting and 3D packing.
On the wire (a request's `mode`, the strategy catalog) `"2d"` / `"3d"`.

polygon.description:
Exterior vertices as [[x, y], ...]: a closed polyline (curves
flattened to vertices before submitting).

quantity.description: Quantity to place: a whole number, at least 1.
Quantity to place: a whole number, at least 1.

LayoutViolationResponse.description:
One way a layout (2D) or packing (3D) breaks its problem. `placement` and
`other` are indices into the response's `placements`; `id` is a geometry
id; a rotation is in degrees and an orientation is its label (`"xzy"`), as
the response gives them.

oneOf.description: The placement names a geometry the problem does not have.
The copy index is not below the geometry's quantity.
A copy is placed a second time.
The rotation is not one the geometry allows.
Flipped, but the geometry does not allow flipping (2D).

An orientation the geometry's `orientation` constraint does not allow
(3D).
In a bin after the first: 3D packs one container.
The packed boxes weigh more than the container's `max_mass` (3D).
A box is not supported as `gravity` or `stability` requires (3D).
On a sheet after the first without `multi_sheet`.
The piece leaves the boundary or comes closer to its edge than `margin`.
Two pieces on one sheet overlap.
Two pieces on one sheet are closer than `spacing`.
Copies are left unplaced but the geometry is not in `unplaced`.
In `unplaced` but every copy is placed, listed twice, or unknown.

Pack3DResponse.description:
3D packing response.

Distinct from [`SolveResponse`] (used for 2D) because the 3D wire contract
differs: bins instead of sheets, and placements carry depth (`z`) and an
`orientation` label. Mirrors the C# `PackingResult` binding
(bindings/csharp/UNesting/Models/Geometry3D.cs).

all_placed.description:
Whether every requested instance was placed. Prefer this over `success`
to detect partial packing. `false` on error responses.

code.description:
Stable name of the reason a request was refused
(`parameter_out_of_range`, `invalid_geometry`, `duplicate_id`, ...);
`null` on success. Branch on this, not on `error`, whose wording may
change.

details.description:
The values behind `code` -- the setting, the geometry id, the
positions; `null` on success.

stop_reason.description:
Why the run stopped: `completed` (the method ran to its own end),
`optimal` (an exact method proved it), `target_reached` (every piece
placed at `target_utilization` or more), `iteration_limit` (the
generation or iteration budget), `no_improvement` (the search stalled),
`time_limit` (`time_limit_ms` ran out -- the layout is the best found
by then) or `cancelled`. `null` on a refusal.

total_requested.description:
Total number of geometry **instances** requested (Σ of every geometry's
quantity). `placements` is instance-level while `unplaced` lists unique
geometry IDs (deduplicated); use `total_requested - placements.len()` to
get the instance-level unplaced count. `0` on error responses.

unplaced.description:
IDs of unplaced geometries (deduplicated). See `unplaced_count` for the
instance-level count.

unplaced_count.description:
Instance-level count of geometry instances that could not be placed
(`total_requested - placements.len()`). Satisfies the invariant
`placements.len() + unplaced_count == total_requested`. `0` on error.

Placement3DResponse.description:
3D placement response.

Mirrors the C# `Placement3D` binding: carries `z` and a string
`orientation` label (e.g. `"xyz"`), and uses `bin_index` (not `sheet_index`).

instance.description: Instance index (0-based) when multiple copies of the same geometry are placed.

orientation.description: Orientation label as an axis permutation, e.g. `"xyz"`, `"xzy"`.

z.description: Z position, along the height axis (the third of `dimensions`).

instance.description: Instance index (0-based) when multiple copies of the same geometry are placed.

RefusalDetails.description:
The values behind a refusal's `code`. Only the ones the reason has are
present.

exclusive_max.description:
Open upper bound of the accepted range: the value must be below it.
Never present together with `max`.

exclusive_min.description:
Open lower bound of the accepted range: the value must be above it.
Never present together with `min`.

expected.description: The names an unknown option could have been.

first.description:
For `duplicate_id`, the position where the id appeared first; `index`
is where it appeared again.

got.description: The value given: a number for a range, a name for an unknown option.

id.description: The geometry the refusal is about.

index.description: The position of the offending entry.

max.description: Closed upper bound of the accepted range: the value may equal it.

min.description: Closed lower bound of the accepted range: the value may equal it.

parameter.description:
The setting or request part at fault (`spacing`, `strategy`,
`geometries`, `max_mass`, ...).

RefusalValue.description: A refused value as it was given.

Request2D.description:
Request for 2D nesting.

All geometry is pre-flattened polylines (vertex arrays): curves (arcs,
Béziers) are flattened to vertices with a tolerance before submitting.
Coordinates are unitless — the caller chooses the unit (e.g. mm), and every
length in a request is in that one unit.

mode.description:
Mode discriminator used by the auto-detect `solve` entry point.
Accepted (and validated) here so a dispatched request round-trips
under the strict unknown-field policy.

Request3D.description:
Request for 3D bin packing.

Boxes and the container are axis-aligned; lengths and masses are unitless
— the caller chooses the units and uses them throughout a request.

mode.description:
Mode discriminator used by the auto-detect `solve` entry point.
Accepted (and validated) here so a dispatched request round-trips
under the strict unknown-field policy.

SkippedContourResponse.description: A contour left out of the cutting sequence.

instance.description: Instance index of the placed geometry.

reason.description:
Why it was left out: `"kerf_collapsed"` -- offsetting by half the kerf
width left nothing (the contour is smaller than the tool).

SolveResponse.description:
Response for solve operations — `solve_2d`'s. The 3D response
(`Pack3DResponse`) has the same shape with `bins_used` for `sheets_used`,
and each placement carries `z` and an orientation.

all_placed.description:
Whether every requested instance was placed
(`placements.len() == total_requested`). Prefer this over `success` to
detect partial packing: `success` only means the solve completed without
error, **not** that all pieces fit. `false` on error responses.

code.description:
Stable name of the reason a request was refused
(`parameter_out_of_range`, `invalid_geometry`, `duplicate_id`, ...);
`null` on success. Branch on this, not on `error`, whose wording may
change.

details.description:
The values behind `code` -- the setting, the geometry id, the
positions; `null` on success.

error.description:
Readable refusal text; `null` on success. Branch on `code`, not on
this text.

stop_reason.description:
Why the run stopped: `completed` (the method ran to its own end),
`optimal` (an exact method proved it), `target_reached` (every piece
placed at `target_utilization` or more), `iteration_limit` (the
generation or iteration budget), `no_improvement` (the search stalled),
`time_limit` (`time_limit_ms` ran out -- the layout is the best found
by then) or `cancelled`. `null` on a refusal.

total_requested.description:
Total number of geometry **instances** requested (Σ of every geometry's
quantity). `placements` is instance-level while `unplaced` lists unique
geometry IDs (deduplicated); use `total_requested - placements.len()` to
get the instance-level unplaced count. `0` on error responses.

unplaced.description:
IDs of unplaced geometries (deduplicated). Tells *which* geometries have
at least one unplaced instance; see `unplaced_count` for *how many*.

unplaced_count.description:
Instance-level count of geometry instances that could not be placed
(`total_requested - placements.len()`). Satisfies the invariant
`placements.len() + unplaced_count == total_requested`. Unlike `unplaced`
(deduplicated IDs), this never undercounts a multi-quantity geometry.
`0` on error responses.

used_bounding_box.description:
Axis-aligned bounding box `[width, height]` of the placed pieces' actual
footprint. Boundary-padding independent, unlike `utilization` (which
divides by the full boundary and shrinks as boundary height grows). For an
open-ended roll the larger axis is the material length consumed.

Populated for **single-sheet** solves (the common open-roll / fabric case),
where all placements share one boundary-local frame. In **multi-sheet**
solves the placements are re-localized per sheet, so a single footprint is
ill-defined and this stays `[0.0, 0.0]`. Also `[0.0, 0.0]` when nothing was
placed or on error.

used_utilization.description:
Utilization against the used bounding box
(`placed_area / (used_width * used_height)`) rather than the full boundary.
A **packing-density** metric: the denominator shrinks on **both** axes to
the placed footprint, so it answers "how tightly are the pieces packed
within their own extent?" independent of boundary padding.

This is **not** a fixed-width stock-efficiency metric. For fixed-width
material (fabric rolls, coil, sheet stock) the boundary width is real
consumed stock, not padding — collapsing the width axis over-reports how
much material was saved. Fixed-width consumers should compute
`placed_area / (boundary_width * used_bounding_box[1])` instead
(`used_bounding_box[1]` is the consumed length and is boundary-independent).

`0.0` when nothing placed, on error, or in multi-sheet solves
(see `used_bounding_box`).

StrategyCatalog.description:
The strategies each dimension offers in this build, and the settings each
reads -- generated from the same table the refusal of an unread setting is
([`Strategy::reads_setting`]), so the two cannot disagree. On the wire:
`{"2d": [{"name": "blf", "reads": ["spacing", ...]}, ...], "3d": [...]}`.

name.description: The strategy's short name, as a request's `config.strategy` takes it.

reads.description:
The `config` settings the strategy reads, in `ConfigRequest::KEYS`
order. A request naming any other setting with this strategy is
refused (`invalid_option`).

available_strategies.input.description: The arguments of available_strategies(), by name; the WebAssembly function takes them in that order.

check_2d.input.description: The arguments of check_2d(request), by name; the WebAssembly function takes them in that order.

check_3d.input.description: The arguments of check_3d(request), by name; the WebAssembly function takes them in that order.

optimize_cutting_path.input.description: The arguments of optimize_cutting_path(request), by name; the WebAssembly function takes them in that order.
